newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUBGY UNION-AUCKLAND HAMMER NATAL SHARKS 39-17.
newsitem.headline: RUBGY UNION-AUCKLAND HAMMER NATAL SHARKS 39-17.

text.p: Reigning Super 12 champions the Auckland Blues held onto their unbroken record by beating a strong Natal Sharks side 39-17 at Eden Park on Sunday.
The Blues took the lead through a Carlos Spencer penalty kick after eight minutes and kept it although the Sharks, losers in last year's final, put up a strong fight for the first hour.
Natal scrum half Kevin Putt showed great anticipation to scoop up a loose ball and run in the first try of the game right between the Auckland posts after 23 minutes.
The home team responded with tries from All Black captain and prop Sean Fitzpatrick and scrum half Ofisa Tonu'u.
Spencer's kicking meant the Blues went into halftime 17-7 up, but the Sharks drew first blood in the second half through a penalty kick from fullback Gavin Lawless.
The Blues found new energy after an ugly incident when power-packed Fijian Joeli Vidiri got 10 minutes in the sin bin for a high tackle on Cabous van der Westhuisen.
Within minutes Spencer scored his fifth try of this year's Super 12 competition before teaming up with the returned Vidiri to overwhelm the Natal defence.
Vidiri grabbed a try, then quickly followed it by winning a fully-justified penalty try, to push the score up to 39-10.
After that the South Africans had little chance of recovery and a well-taken John Slade try in injury time was their only consolation.

Auckland Blues: 15-Shane Howarth, 14-Joeli Vidiri, 13-Eroni Clarke, 12-Lee Stensness, 11-Jeremy Stanley, 10-Carlos Spencer, 9-Ofisa Tonu'u, 8-Zinzan Brooke (captain), 7-Mark Carter, 6-Dylan Mika, 5-Leo Lafaiali'i, 4-Robin Brooke, 3-Craig Dowd (Orcades Crawford), 2-Sean Fitzpatrick, 1-Paul Thomson.

Natal Sharks: 15-Gavin Lawless, 14-Jeremy Thomson, 13-Piet Muller, 12-Joos Joubert, 11-Cabous van der Westhuizen (Dirkie Strydom), 10-Henry Honiball, 9-Kevin Putt, 8-Gary Teichmann (captain), 7-Wayne Fyvie, 6-Wickus van Heerden, 5-Mark Andrews, 4-John Slade, 3-Adrian Garvey, 2-John Allan, 1-Rob Kempson.
